title: A Time Capsule for America's 250th Birthday!
summary:
On July 4, 2026, the United States will celebrate its 250th birthday! To mark the occasion, officials are burying a time capsule in Philadelphia. It's designed to give future Americans a peek at life in 2026. The capsule won't be opened until July 4, 2276—that's 250 years from now, when the nation turns 500!

All 50 states, plus Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories, contributed items. Some states went all out. Utah sent 100 cards, 13 coins, 8 documents, 8 pins, 2 granite disks, and a booklet. Arkansas submitted a diamond. Maine added a bone from an endangered whale. Wisconsin contributed a feather from "Old Abe," a bald eagle that served with Union soldiers during the Civil War. California sent a computer chip and an AI-generated prediction of what the state might look like in 2276.

But choosing the items was only half the challenge. Making sure they survive underground for 250 years was even harder. That job went to Michael Berilla and his team at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Berilla said the capsule is so well-sealed that "Philadelphia would have to be six feet underwater for it to even possibly take on water."

The capsule will be buried near Independence Hall in Philadelphia, where the Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776. To help future generations find it, a special sculpture will mark the spot. It's shaped like a large segmented snake, inspired by Benjamin Franklin's famous "Join, or Die" cartoon. The National Park Service has also recorded the location in official documents.

When the capsule is opened in 2276, the first things people will see are a photo of the engineering team and a letter from Berilla. It says, "Greetings from the living, breathing hearts and hands of 2026. We will have long since returned to dust, but our devotion, pride, and unwavering hope for what our world could become are alive right here inside this steel. We built this for you."

Wow! Imagine what people 250 years from now will think when they open it!
why_it_matters: This time capsule is like a message to the future, showing kids today that what they do and create could be remembered and celebrated by people hundreds of years from now.

background_read: Independence Hall in Philadelphia is where the Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776, declaring America's freedom from British rule.
Benjamin Franklin (one of America's Founding Fathers) drew the 'Join, or Die' cartoon to encourage the colonies to unite, and it became a symbol of togetherness.
Time capsules have been used for centuries to preserve objects for future people, giving them a snapshot of life in a different era.
Article_Structure: WHO: All 50 states, U.S. territories, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) team led by Michael Berilla.
WHAT: They gathered items and built a highly sealed time capsule to bury for America's 250th birthday, not to be opened for 250 more years.
WHERE: Buried near Independence Hall in Philadelphia.
WHY: To give Americans in 2276 a glimpse into life in 2026 and celebrate the nation's long history.

perspectives.description: They are excited to share their unique culture and history, hoping future generations will understand what life was like in their state.
They focus on the challenge of keeping the items safe from water and decay, ensuring the capsule survives centuries.
They will open the capsule with curiosity, amazed by objects from the past and the letter of hope from 2026.
